title: CPSC, Sassy Announce Voluntary Recall to Remove Squirting Fish from Bath Toys
product: Scoop Pour 'N Squirt squirting fish bath toy
reason: The fish's size, texture, shape and easy compressibility make it possible for an infant to compress the toy and place it in his or her mouth. If the toy reaches the back of the mouth and expands, it may block the child's airway.
distribution: Mass merchandise stores and toy stores sold these toys nationwide, from February 1999 to December 2000, for about $5.
hazards: The fish's size, texture, shape and easy compressibility make it possible for an infant to compress the toy and place it in his or her mouth. If the toy reaches the back of the mouth and expands, it may block the child's airway.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take these squirting fish away from young children and throw them away.
injuries: CPSC and Sassy are aware of one report of an infant who put the toy fish in his mouth gagged and vomited and two other reports of infants who put the toy fish in their mouths and started to choke. Sassy is working cooperatively with the CPSC in taking action to correct this problem.

title: CPSC, Cenex Harvest States Cooperatives Announce Recall to Inspect Propane Gas
reason: The propane may not have contained enough odorant to allow consumers to smell leaking gas, presenting a fire, explosion or thermal burn hazard to consumers.
firm: Cenex Harvest States Cooperatives (CHS), of Inver Grove Heights, Minn.
hazards: The propane may not have contained enough odorant to allow consumers to smell leaking gas, presenting a fire, explosion or thermal burn hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers who had propane deliveries or purchased propane from these dealers since June 1, 2000, should immediately contact their propane gas suppliers or retail locations, where portable cylinders were filled to arrange for testing of the propane. The amount of odorant in the propane can be corrected on-site if the levels are found to be too low to detect by smell.
injuries: CHS learned of two explosions involving propane gas in Montana, that resulted in four injuries.

title: Christmas Trees Recalled by Walgreen
product: Professional Series Fiber Optic 3 ft. Tree
reason: A color wheel in the tree stand, that is used to light the trees can overheat and catch fire.
distribution: Walgreens nationwide sold the trees this holiday season for about $40.
hazards: A color wheel in the tree stand, that is used to light the trees can overheat and catch fire.
remedies: Stop using the trees immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
injuries: Two reports of the color wheel overheating and melting. No injuries were reported.

title: Christmas Lights Recalled by Sun Sun Industries
reason: The lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and light sockets, posing electric shock and fire hazards to consumers.
distribution: The lights were sold in M&S Bargain Hunter stores throughout New York, from October 2000 to December 2000, for about $2.
hazards: The lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and light sockets, posing electric shock and fire hazards to consumers.
remedies: Stop using the lights immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

title: Christmas Lights Recalled by Pioneer Paper Co.
reason: The lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and light sockets, posing electric shock and fire hazards to consumers.
distribution: The lights were sold at discount stores throughout New York, from September 2000 to December 2000, for about $6.
hazards: The lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and light sockets, posing electric shock and fire hazards to consumers.
remedies: Stop using the lights immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

title: Christmas Lights Recalled by GEM Stores
product: Miniature Christmas lights and icicle-style lights
reason: The lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and light sockets, posing electric shock and fire hazards to consumers.
distribution: The lights were sold in GEM stores throughout New York, from November 2000 to December 2000.
hazards: The lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and light sockets, posing electric shock and fire hazards to consumers.
remedies: Stop using the lights immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

title: CPSC, White Outdoor Products Co. Announce Recall of Lawn and Garden Tractors
reason: The hood latch on these tractors can damage the fuel tank and cause fuel to leak when the hood is raised and lowered, presenting a fire and explosion hazard.
firm: White Outdoor Products Co., (a subsidiary of MTD Products Inc.) of Cleveland, Ohio
distribution: White Outdoor Products Co. dealers nationwide sold the tractors, from November 1999 through December 2000, for between $1,600 and $3,400.
hazards: The hood latch on these tractors can damage the fuel tank and cause fuel to leak when the hood is raised and lowered, presenting a fire and explosion hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled tractors immediately and contact White Outdoor Products Co. to verify their unit is part of the recall. If recalled, consumers will receive a replacement hood latch and fuel tank inspection instructions.
injuries: White Outdoor Products Co. has received one report of the hood latch damaging the fuel tank. No reports of fuel leaks, fires or injuries have been received.

title: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of "Ranger" Strollers
product: Kolcraft Ranger and Ranger Quattro strollers
reason: Lock mechanisms, found on both sides of the stroller, can break and create a pinch-point hazard. Young children can be injured when their fingers, arms or hands are pinched between parts of the locking mechanism.
distribution: Mass merchandise and juvenile products stores nationwide sold these strollers, January 2000 through November 2000, for about $80.
hazards: Lock mechanisms, found on both sides of the stroller, can break and create a pinch-point hazard. Young children can be injured when their fingers, arms or hands are pinched between parts of the locking mechanism.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the strollers immediately and call Kolcraft to receive a free repair kit.
injuries: Kolcraft has received 39 reports of the lock mechanisms breaking, including one report of a baby's arm being pinched.

title: CPSC, Excite Ltd. Announce Recall of Scooters
product: Excite Super Speeder II and Viper scooter
reason: The front of the folding mechanism, where the steering column meets the base of the scooter, can create a pinch-point. Fingers can be injured while folding or unfolding the scooter.
firm: Excite Ltd., of Hong Kong
distribution: Rite Aid stores nationwide exclusively sold the Super Speeder II and Viper scooters, from August 2000 to December 2000, for about $49.
hazards: The front of the folding mechanism, where the steering column meets the base of the scooter, can create a pinch-point. Fingers can be injured while folding or unfolding the scooter.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these Excite scooters immediately and contact Excite Ltd. to receive a free cap that will cover the front of the folding mechanism.
injuries: Excite has received nine reports of pinch-point injuries to children including one partially amputated fingertip and eight lacerations, one of which required eight stitches.

title: CPSC, DEWALT® Industrial Tool Co. Announce Recall of Battery Chargers
product: DEWALT and Black & Decker battery chargers used with cordless power tools
reason: The battery charger can fail to automatically shut off after the battery is fully charged, which can cause the battery to burst, and poses fire, burn and electrical shock hazards to consumers.
distribution: Home center and hardware stores sold these battery chargers nationwide, from May 1996 through August 2000, for between $50 and $60. During the same time, these chargers also were sold with some DEWALT® and Black & Decker Industry & Construction cordless tools.
hazards: The battery charger can fail to automatically shut off after the battery is fully charged, which can cause the battery to burst, and poses fire, burn and electrical shock hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these battery chargers immediately, and take them to a DEWALT or Black & Decker service center for a free replacement.
injuries: DEWALT has received two reports of batteries bursting and consumers suffering injuries, including minor lacerations and a minor burn.

title: CPSC, L. Powell Co. Announces Recall of Glider Rockers
reason: These glider rockers were manufactured improperly with soft wood and with nails, rather than with wood screws in the gliding joints. The glider rockers can break apart, causing occupants to fall to the floor.
distribution: Fingerhut mail order, furniture stores and specialty shops nationwide sold these glider rockers with and without an accompanying ottoman, from November 1999 to September 2000, for up to $145.
hazards: These glider rockers were manufactured improperly with soft wood and with nails, rather than with wood screws in the gliding joints. The glider rockers can break apart, causing occupants to fall to the floor.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the glider rockers, and contact L. Powell to receive a free repair kit to stabilize the rocker. Consumers were sent direct notification of this recall.
injuries: L. Powell has received 44 reports of glider rockers breaking and causing consumers to fall, 12 of which involved minor injuries, such as scratches and bruises.

title: CPSC, Emerson Motor Co. Recall Dayton Motors
reason: If the motor is not properly grounded as instructed, the motor could become energized and cause a shock or electrocution hazard, resulting in injury or death.
firm: The Emerson Motor Co., of St. Louis, Mo.
distribution: These motors were sold directly through motor distributors or repair shops, from October 1999 through August 2000, for about $95.
hazards: If the motor is not properly grounded as instructed, the motor could become energized and cause a shock or electrocution hazard, resulting in injury or death.
remedies: Consumers, with the recalled motor, should unplug it and remove it from service and contact Dayton Motor Hotline for repair information. Notices have been sent to known purchasers.

title: CPSC and GE Announce Free Repair Supplement of Rebate Program for Recalled Dishwashers: Recalled Units Still Being Used, Creating Risk of Fire
reason: The dishwashers have a slide switch that can melt and ignite, presenting a fire hazard.
firm: General Electric Appliances Co., of Louisville, Ky.
hazards: The dishwashers have a slide switch that can melt and ignite, presenting a fire hazard.
remedies: Both the CPSC and GE strongly urge consumers who have not replaced their recalled units under the original rebate program to contact GE right away to schedule a free rewiring or participate in the original rebate program. Until the dishwasher has been rewired, consumers should keep the dishwasher door unlatched at all times to prevent the flow of electrical current that creates a risk of fire. With the free rewire option, a GE-authorized technician will rewire the slide switch at no cost to consumers. This supplements the original rebate program announced October 19, 1999.
injuries: There have been approximately 90 incidents of fire, smoking and melted switches, 14 of which included fires that spread beyond the dishwasher. Approximately 10 incidents have occurred since the recall announcement. No injuries have been reported.

title: Stuffed Toys Recalled by Pier 1 Imports
reason: The toys have small parts, which could come loose, posing a possible choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Pier 1 Imports stores nationwide sold these toys, from August 2000 through October 2000, for about $6.
hazards: The toys have small parts, which could come loose, posing a possible choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.

title: Candle Holders Recalled by ATICO International USA
reason: The plastic marshmallow can ignite when it is used with a burning candle, presenting a fire and burn hazard.
distribution: TOPS stores in New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio sold the candle holders during the month of September 2000 for about $5.
hazards: The plastic marshmallow can ignite when it is used with a burning candle, presenting a fire and burn hazard.
remedies: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
injuries: ATICO International USA Inc. has received two reports of fires. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall of Additional 170,000 Busy Poppin' Pals Toys
product: Sesame Street Busy Poppin' Pals toys
reason: Small springs inside these toys can break loose, posing a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
distribution: Mass merchandise stores and toy stores sold these toys (Playskool model 5446 made in China) nationwide, from November 1994 through 1996, for about $10.
hazards: Small springs inside these toys can break loose, posing a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and contact Playskool to get information about how to receive a free redesigned replacement toy.
injuries: Playskool has received eight reports relating to the springs in its Sesame Street Busy Poppin' Pals toys, including one report that a child put the broken spring in his mouth. No injuries were reported. Playskool received 16 reports of springs breaking in the Busy Poppin' Pals toy recalled earlier. This resulted in five children putting the broken springs in their mouths, and two of these children suffering lacerations.

title: CPSC, LeapFrog Announce Recall to Repair "Alphabet Pal" Educational Pull Toys
product: Leap Frog "Alphabet Pal" electronic pull toys
reason: The toy has a two-part red plastic connector on the pull string, designed to separate under tension. The plastic pieces can detach from the string when the connector is pulled apart and could pose a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Toy, department and specialty stores nationwide sold these toys, from June 1999 through November 2000, for about $20.
hazards: The toy has a two-part red plastic connector on the pull string, designed to separate under tension. The plastic pieces can detach from the string when the connector is pulled apart and could pose a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should cut the red plastic string connector off of these toys immediately, or return it to the firm to receive a free replacement toy without a plastic connector.
injuries: LeapFrog has received nine reports of the red plastic connector detaching. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Kent International and Kash 'N Gold Ltd. Announce Recall of Scooters
product: Kent Kickin' Mini-Scooters and Kash 'N Gold Racer X20TM Scooters
reason: The Kent scooter handles can unexpectedly come out of the steering column if the clamp holding them in is not tight, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries. For the Kash 'N Gold scooters, the plastic "T" joint between the handlebars can break, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries.
distribution: Discovery and Mervyn's stores sold these scooters nationwide, from August 2000 through September 2000, for between $70 and $100.
hazards: The Kent scooter handles can unexpectedly come out of the steering column if the clamp holding them in is not tight, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries. For the Kash 'N Gold scooters, the plastic "T" joint between the handlebars can break, causing the rider to lose control, fall and possibly suffer injuries.
remedies: Kent: Consumers should stop riding these Kent scooters immediately, and call Kent International to receive a free replacement handlebar with pins to secure the handlebars. Kash 'N Gold: Consumers should stop riding these scooters immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or a new scooter with a metal "T" joint.
injuries: Kent has received four reports of the handles coming out, resulting in four children suffering injuries, including broken arms, a broken wrist, bruises, abrasions and a cracked tooth.

title: CPSC, DiaTech USA and Derby USA Announce Recall of Bicycles
product: Disc bakes on DiaTech 2000 model bicycles
reason: The disc brakes on these bicycles can stick and prevent the brake pads from returning to the proper position, when the brake lever is released. This can cause the rider to lose control and crash.
firm: DiaTech USA, of Kenmore, Wash.
distribution: Raleigh, Diamondback and Univega bicycle dealers nationwide sold these bicycles, from November 1999 through June 2000, for between $800 and $1,200.
hazards: The disc brakes on these bicycles can stick and prevent the brake pads from returning to the proper position, when the brake lever is released. This can cause the rider to lose control and crash.
remedies: Consumers should stop riding these bicycles immediately, and return them to their dealer for free replacement of the front and rear brake calipers.
injuries: DiaTech USA, the manufacturer of the brakes, and Derby USA, the importer and distributor, have received one report of a consumer who lost control of his bicycle when the brakes failed to disengage, and suffered broken ribs.

title: CPSC and Small Beginnings Inc. Announce Recall of "Pacee" Pacifiers
reason: The pacifiers failed CPSC testing standards. These pacifiers present a choking hazard to infants.
firm: Small Beginnings Inc., of Hesperia, Calif.
distribution: Various hospitals and medical supply distributors sold these pacifiers nationwide, from October 1999 through April 2000, for about $1.
hazards: The pacifiers failed CPSC testing standards. These pacifiers present a choking hazard to infants.
remedies: Consumers should take the pacifiers away from infants immediately, and return them to the firm for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and Small Beginnings are not aware of any injuries involving these pacifiers. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Profile Design Announce Recall of Bicycle Handlebar Stems
reason: The stem connects the bicycle's handlebars to the fork. These stems can break during use, causing the bicycle rider to crash and suffer serious injuries.
firm: Profile Design LLC, of Carson, Calif.
distribution: Independent bicycle dealers nationwide sold bicycles and parts kits with these stems and individual stems, from March 1997 through April 2000. The stems sold for about $50.
hazards: The stem connects the bicycle's handlebars to the fork. These stems can break during use, causing the bicycle rider to crash and suffer serious injuries.
remedies: Consumers should stop using bicycles with these stems immediately, and either call Profile Design to get a free replacement stem, or return the bicycle with the recalled stem to a Profile-Design retailer, to have the stem replaced free of charge.
injuries: Profile Design has received reports of six riders crashing when the stems on their bicycles broke, resulting in teeth injuries, bruises and abrasions.

title: CPSC, Lifetime Hoan Corp. Announce Recall of Fondue Sets to Replace Burners
reason: Some sets have alcohol burners that can produce high flames beyond the intended-cooking surface of the fondue pot. Another set, which uses chafing fuel, is being recalled because the chafing fuel holder could tip as it burns down. Both problems present potential fire and burn hazards to consumers.
firm: Lifetime Hoan Corp., of Westbury, N.Y.
distribution: Department, kitchen and home stores nationwide sold the fondue sets, from June 1999 through October 2000, for about $20.
hazards: Some sets have alcohol burners that can produce high flames beyond the intended-cooking surface of the fondue pot. Another set, which uses chafing fuel, is being recalled because the chafing fuel holder could tip as it burns down. Both problems present potential fire and burn hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the burners immediately and contact the company to find out how to dispose of the burners. Consumers with recalled alcohol burners will be sent a $4 coupon toward the purchase of Sterno® canned chafing fuel.
injuries: CPSC and Lifetime Hoan Corp. have received eight reports of burners producing high flames. No injuries or property damage has been reported.

title: CPSC, Stack-On Products Co. Announce Recall of Gun Cabinets
reason: The gun cabinets have push button locks that can be opened without the use of a key, allowing unauthorized access to firearms.
firm: Stack-On Products Co., of Wauconda, Ill.
distribution: Outdoor and sporting good stores nationwide sold the Stack-On brand cabinets and Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. nationwide exclusively sold Sentinel brand cabinets from May 2000 through September 2000. These gun cabinets sold for between $240 and $300.
hazards: The gun cabinets have push button locks that can be opened without the use of a key, allowing unauthorized access to firearms.
remedies: Consumers with these gun cabinets should contact Stack-On Products for information on receiving a free push button replacement lock.
injuries: Stack-On Products has received two reports of consumers being able to open locks without using their keys. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Cosco Announce Recall to Repair High Chairs
reason: The high chairs are adjustable and have both recline and upright positions. In the recline position, the seats can separate from the frame and fall to the ground. In the upright position, the seats can slip from their set height position to the lowest position or can fall to the ground. Additionally, some seats were sold with a metal restraint anchor that can slip through the back of the seat, allowing the child to fall to the ground. Infants and toddlers can suffer head, face and bodily injuries.
firm: Cosco Inc., of Columbus, Ind.
distribution: The Options 5 High Chairs subject to this recall were manufactured from December 1, 1997 through August 11, 2000. Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount department stores nationwide sold the high chairs for about $40 to $50.
hazards: The high chairs are adjustable and have both recline and upright positions. In the recline position, the seats can separate from the frame and fall to the ground. In the upright position, the seats can slip from their set height position to the lowest position or can fall to the ground. Additionally, some seats were sold with a metal restraint anchor that can slip through the back of the seat, allowing the child to fall to the ground. Infants and toddlers can suffer head, face and bodily injuries.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these high chairs immediately. Repair kits are no longer available. New cash incentive is being offered or replacement product. Do not use these products. Please discard or destroy these products.
injuries: Cosco and CPSC have received 168 reports of incidents involving the high chairs' seats or restraints, including 57 injury reports, primarily to the head and face. Two children reportedly suffered slight concussions; twelve children were monitored for head injuries; and others suffered swollen eyes, bloody noses and lips, bumps and bruises.

title: CPSC, Cooper Lighting Announce Recall of Recessed Lights
product: Halo Brand Metropolitan Ice Series #945 and #1945 recessed lights
reason: The glass ring exterior portion or trim of these lights can fall from the fixture, posing a risk of lacerations and impact injuries.
firm: Cooper Lighting, of Elk Grove Village, Ill.
distribution: Home Depot catalogs, electricians, and electrical supply companies sold these lights nationwide, from September 1996 through October 2000, for about $40.
hazards: The glass ring exterior portion or trim of these lights can fall from the fixture, posing a risk of lacerations and impact injuries.
remedies: Consumers with the recalled lights will receive free replacement trims. The firm will send consumers free shipping labels to return the trims.
injuries: Cooper Lighting has received four reports of glass rings falling from these light fixtures. In two incidents, consumers were hit on the head, causing lacerations and bumps.

title: Power Strips and Extension Cords Recalled by Howard Berger
reason: The power strips have undersized wires, lack over-current protection and grounding, and the plastic case is flammable. The extension cords have undersized wires and lack over-current protection. Both the power strips and the extension cords can overheat, presenting electrocution, shock and fire hazards.
distribution: Discount stores in the eastern United States and Puerto Rico sold these products, from September 1998 to September 2000.
hazards: The power strips have undersized wires, lack over-current protection and grounding, and the plastic case is flammable. The extension cords have undersized wires and lack over-current protection. Both the power strips and the extension cords can overheat, presenting electrocution, shock and fire hazards.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these products immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

title: Desk Fans Recalled by Morton Paper Co.
reason: The fans could overheat during use, and do not have sufficient guards to prevent possible finger entrapment. These fans present electrocution, shock, fire, and finger amputation hazards.
distribution: Discount stores in the metropolitan New York area sold these electric fans, from April 1999 through June 2000, for about $20.
hazards: The fans could overheat during use, and do not have sufficient guards to prevent possible finger entrapment. These fans present electrocution, shock, fire, and finger amputation hazards.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these fans immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
injuries: None reported

title: CPSC, Small Small World Announce Recall of Plush Rabbit Toy
product: Plush rabbit toys: Natalie Nibblenose and Nickie Nibblenose
reason: The eyes on these toys could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Specialty stores sold these toys nationwide, from December 1999 through September 2000, for about $6.
hazards: The eyes on these toys could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased, for a free replacement toy.
injuries: Small Small World has not received any reports of injuries associated with these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Kawasaki Motors Corp. Announce Recall of Off-Road Motorcycles
reason: A frame down tube on these motorcycles can crack below the steering head. Use of the motorcycle with a cracked down tube can result in failure of the frame, which can cause the rider to lose control of the motorcycle and crash, resulting in injury or death.
firm: Kawasaki Motors Corp. U.S.A., of Irvine, Calif.
distribution: Kawasaki dealers nationwide sold these motorcycles, from November 1999 through October 2000, for about $2,700.
hazards: A frame down tube on these motorcycles can crack below the steering head. Use of the motorcycle with a cracked down tube can result in failure of the frame, which can cause the rider to lose control of the motorcycle and crash, resulting in injury or death.
remedies: Consumers with the recalled motorcycles should stop using them immediately and call their local Kawasaki dealer to schedule a free inspection and repair.
injuries: Kawasaki has received 60 reports of frames on these motorcycles cracking. Three of these incidents reportedly resulted in the down tube failing, leading to crashes. Injuries to riders included broken bones and abrasions.

title: CPSC, Honda Announce Recall of Off-Road Motorcycles
product: Year 2000 and 2001 Honda XR50R off-road motorcycles
reason: The two bolts that attach the handlebars can break. If the handlebars separate from the motorcycle, the rider loses steering control and can crash, posing the risk of serious injuries.
firm: American Honda Motor Co. Inc., of Torrance Calif.
distribution: Honda motorcycle dealers nationwide sold these motorcycles, from September 1999 through October 2000, for about $1,300.
hazards: The two bolts that attach the handlebars can break. If the handlebars separate from the motorcycle, the rider loses steering control and can crash, posing the risk of serious injuries.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these motorcycles immediately, and call their local Honda motorcycle dealer to schedule a free repair.
injuries: Honda has received four reports of handlebars separating from these motorcycles. No injuries have been reported. Honda also received four reports of loose handlebars caused by one of the two bolts failing.

title: CPSC, L.L. Bean Inc. Announce Recall of Toddlers' Slippers
reason: The drawcord around the ankle of these slippers can break and release the toggle used to tighten the drawcord. The toggle presents a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: The L.L. Kids Store in Freeport, Maine, the L.L. Bean Store in McLean, Va., and the L.L. Bean catalogs and web site sold the slippers nationwide, from August 2000 through October 2000, for about $18.
hazards: The drawcord around the ankle of these slippers can break and release the toggle used to tighten the drawcord. The toggle presents a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these slippers away from young children immediately, and return them to L.L. Bean for an exchange or refund.
injuries: L.L. Bean has received one report of a 12 month-old baby pulling the toggle off of his slipper. No injuries were reported.

title: CPSC, General Binding Corp. Announce Recall of Paper Shredders
reason: These paper shredders do not have a protective shield to guard against exposure to the cutting blades. Consumers could lift the paper shredder lid while it is running and come into contact with the turning blades. Consumers could suffer cuts or amputations of finger tips, if they touch the turning blades.
distribution: Office supply stores nationwide sold these paper shredders, from August 2000 through September 2000, for about $139.
hazards: These paper shredders do not have a protective shield to guard against exposure to the cutting blades. Consumers could lift the paper shredder lid while it is running and come into contact with the turning blades. Consumers could suffer cuts or amputations of finger tips, if they touch the turning blades.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled paper shredders immediately, and call GBC to receive a free replacement paper shredder or a refund.
injuries: GBC is not aware of any injuries involving these paper shredders. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Three Firms Announce Recall of Bicycle Helmets
product: Variflex Inc. "X-Games Aggressive" Bicycle Helmets, NHS TSG Helmets, and First Team Sports "Guardian Junior Helmets"
reason: These helmets fail impact testing required under CPSC's Safety Standard for Bicycle Helmets, violating the Consumer Product Safety Act. Riders wearing these helmets are not adequately protected from falls, and could suffer severe head injuries or death.
distribution: Sporting good and discount department stores nationwide sold the Variflex Inc. "X-Games Aggressive" helmets, from October 1999 through September 2000, for about $20. Sporting good stores nationwide sold the NHS TSG helmets, from February 2000 through October 2000, for between $35 and $45. Sporting goods stores in the eastern and north eastern U.S. sold the First Team Sports "Guardian Junior" helmets, from February 2000 through October 2000, for about $25.
hazards: These helmets fail impact testing required under CPSC's Safety Standard for Bicycle Helmets, violating the Consumer Product Safety Act. Riders wearing these helmets are not adequately protected from falls, and could suffer severe head injuries or death.
remedies: Variflex Inc.: Consumers should stop using these helmets immediately, and return them to the store where purchased, for a refund or replacement helmet. NHS: Consumers should stop using these helmets immediately and return them to NHS Inc., not to the store where purchased, for a refund. First Team Sports: Consumers should stop using these helmets immediately, and return them to the store where purchased, for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and these firms are not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these helmets.

title: Electric Fans Recalled by Agis Enterprises Co.
product: Electric fans: a 12-inch desk fan, a 16-inch desk fan, a 16-inch stand fan, an 18- inch stand fan with three legs, and an 18-inch stand fan with a round base
reason: The fans could overheat during use, present an electrocution hazard and do not have sufficient guards to prevent fingers from contacting the fan blades, posing the risk of finger amputations.
firm: Agis Enterprises Co. Inc., of West Keansburg, N.J.
distribution: Discount stores in the metropolitan New York area sold these electric fans, from April 1998 through September 1999, for about $50.
hazards: The fans could overheat during use, present an electrocution hazard and do not have sufficient guards to prevent fingers from contacting the fan blades, posing the risk of finger amputations.
remedies: Stop using these fans immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.

title: Curious George Musical Pull Toys Recalled by Prestige Toy Corp.
reason: The toy has two elastic cords that form a loop, posing a strangulation risk to young children.
firm: Prestige Toy Corp., of New York, N.Y.
distribution: Kmart stores nationwide sold these toys, from June 1999 through September 1999, for about $10.
hazards: The toy has two elastic cords that form a loop, posing a strangulation risk to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using this toy immediately and return it to Kmart, for a replacement toy.
injuries: Prestige Toy Corp. has received a report of a child found with the cords of the toy wrapped around his neck. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Emerson Tool Co. Announce Recall of Craftsman® Radial Arm Saws Sold by Sears, Roebuck and Co.
reason: These radial arm saws were sold without a guard that covers the entire blade. Consumers have come into contact with the blade or have been hit by pieces of wood kicked back by the saws, resulting in severe injuries.

injuries: CPSC and Vaid Enterprises are not aware of any injuries involving these cigarette lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Replace Infant Toys
reason: The toy's brightly colored end knobs can detach and allow small geometric-shaped pieces to come loose, posing a choking hazard to infants and young children.
distribution: Toy and mass merchandise stores, including Toys "R" Us and Wal- Mart, sold these toys, from October 1997 through September 2000, for about $8.
hazards: The toy's brightly colored end knobs can detach and allow small geometric-shaped pieces to come loose, posing a choking hazard to infants and young children.
remedies: Parents and caregivers should take the toy away from infants and young children immediately, and contact Playskool to receive a free redesigned replacement toy.
injuries: Playskool has received 10 reports of the toy's knobs detaching to release small parts, including four reports of a small part from the toy being found in the mouths of infants and young children. There have been no reported injuries.

title: CPSC, Kawasaki Announce Recall of All-Terrain Vehicles
reason: Under certain conditions, the drive belts on these ATVs can break, and pieces of the belt can lock up the transmission, including the wheels, causing the vehicle to stop suddenly. This can cause the operator to lose control of the vehicle, crash, or be ejected off the vehicle, resulting in injury or death.
firm: Kawasaki Motors Corp. U.S.A., of Irvine, Calif.
distribution: Kawasaki dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from September 1996 through August 2000, for between $5,300 and $6,200.
hazards: Under certain conditions, the drive belts on these ATVs can break, and pieces of the belt can lock up the transmission, including the wheels, causing the vehicle to stop suddenly. This can cause the operator to lose control of the vehicle, crash, or be ejected off the vehicle, resulting in injury or death.
remedies: Consumers with the recalled ATVs should stop using them immediately, and call their Kawasaki dealer to schedule a free belt inspection. Original equipment belts will be replaced with a new generation belt free of charge. Also, an addendum to the owner's manual and a warning label about maintaining the drive belt will be provided.
injuries: Kawasaki has received reports of 12 riders suffering injuries as a result of drive belts breaking and their vehicle suddenly stopping.

title: CPSC, API Outdoors Announce Recall of Hunting Treestands and Treeseats
reason: The seat of these devices can collapse, causing the consumer to fall to the ground and suffer injury.
firm: API Outdoors, a division of Outland Sports Inc., of Tallulah, La.
distribution: Hunting supply stores and catalogs nationwide sold the treestands and treeseats, from January 1999 through August 2000. Prices for the treestands were between $60 and $90, and prices for the treeseats were between $30 and $40.
hazards: The seat of these devices can collapse, causing the consumer to fall to the ground and suffer injury.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled treestands and treeseats immediately, and contact API Outdoors for a free repair.
injuries: CPSC and API Outdoors are not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these products. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Tek Nek Toys Announce Recall of Children's Riding Vehicles
reason: The vehicles' battery charger or wires can overheat, presenting fire and injury hazards to children.
distribution: Toy stores and discount department stores sold the vehicles nationwide, from July 1998 through April 2000, for about $89.
hazards: The vehicles' battery charger or wires can overheat, presenting fire and injury hazards to children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the vehicles immediately and contact Tek Nek to receive a free, new charger. Consumers should not charge the vehicles or let children use the vehicles until they have received the new charger.
injuries: CPSC and Tek Nek have received 17 reports of battery chargers and wires overheating, while vehicles were being charged. Two consumers burned their hands while unplugging or charging the vehicles.

title: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Children's Riding Vehicles
reason: The foot pedals, which activate the ride-ons, can stick in the "on" position. Children can be injured when the motorcycle ride-ons fail to stop and strike other objects.
firm: Fisher-Price, of East Aurora, N.Y.
distribution: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores, and Harley-Davidson dealerships sold the motorcycle ride-ons nationwide, from September 1999 through August 2000, for about $190 for the red vehicle and $700 for the black vehicle.
hazards: The foot pedals, which activate the ride-ons, can stick in the "on" position. Children can be injured when the motorcycle ride-ons fail to stop and strike other objects.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these motorcycle ride-ons immediately, and call Fisher-Price to determine if your vehicle is part of this recall. Consumers with recalled ride-ons will receive a free foot pedal repair kit. The repair can be easily completed in the home.
injuries: Fisher-Price has received nine reports of the foot pedal on these vehicles sticking. One 3-year-old boy suffered cuts and bruises when his motorcycle ride-ons ran into a home.

title: CPSC, Empire Industries Announce Recall of Children's Riding Vehicles
product: "Power Drivers" and "Buddy L" battery-powered children's riding vehicles
reason: The vehicles' battery chargers can overheat, presenting fire and injury hazards to children.
firm: Empire Industries, of Tarboro, N.C.
distribution: Toy stores and retail catalogs sold the vehicles nationwide, from July 1995 through December 1997, for about $130 to $250.
hazards: The vehicles' battery chargers can overheat, presenting fire and injury hazards to children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the vehicles immediately. Empire Industries is no longer in business and cannot provide charger adapters or other replacement parts. Consumers should discontinue use of these products, and discard or destroy them.
injuries: CPSC and Empire have received about 100 reports of chargers overheating, melting or burning. Five house fires have been reported, resulting in at least $100,000 in property damage. One child and one adult received burns to hands on overheated charger jacks.

title: CPSC, R4 Technical Center Announce Recall of Propane Cylinders
reason: These cylinders can have missing or damaged internal seals in the cylinder valves. Propane can leak, posing a risk of fire, explosion and burn injuries.
firm: R4 Technical Center - North Carolina LLC, of Hamptonville, N.C.
distribution: Home center, discount department and hardware stores, and gas stations in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, West Virginia, Florida and Mississippi sold these propane cylinders, from May 2000 through July 2000, for about $40 to $60 for a tank or $13 to $16 for a tank exchange.
hazards: These cylinders can have missing or damaged internal seals in the cylinder valves. Propane can leak, posing a risk of fire, explosion and burn injuries.
remedies: Consumers with the recalled valves should check for leaks by following the "Connection Instructions" on the cylinder's label. If the valve is leaking, turn it off immediately, and call the R4 Technical Center to receive a free replacement cylinder.
injuries: R4 Technical Center has not received any reports of injuries.

title: CPSC, KinderkidsTM Announce Recall of Inflatable Playrings for Babies
reason: When a baby leans his face against the side of the playring, the soft surface covers the baby's nose and mouth, restricting airflow, and posing the risk of suffocation.
distribution: Walmart stores, and One Step Ahead, a mail-order company, sold the playrings, from July 1998 through April 2000, for between $20 and $35.
hazards: When a baby leans his face against the side of the playring, the soft surface covers the baby's nose and mouth, restricting airflow, and posing the risk of suffocation.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the playrings immediately and discard or destroy these products. The firm is out of business and cannot be contacted, and a refund is no longer available.
injuries: CPSC has received one report of a 6-month old baby found gasping for air after falling asleep face down in the playring. The baby was removed from the playring without injury. CPSC is aware of infant suffocation deaths when their airflow is restricted from contact with soft surfaces.

title: CPSC, Fazoli's Announce Recall of Toys Included with Kids Meals
product: Pasta Pals toys included with Fazoli's Kids Meals
reason: The bottom of the container can fit over a child's nose and mouth, which could pose a suffocation hazard to children under 3 years of age.
distribution: Fazoli's restaurants nationwide included the Pasta Pals toys with Fazoli's Kids Meals from January 2000 through August 2000.
hazards: The bottom of the container can fit over a child's nose and mouth, which could pose a suffocation hazard to children under 3 years of age.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the barrel-shaped container away from young children. Discard the container or return it to any Fazoli's restaurant for a free Italian Lemon Ice.
injuries: Fazoli's has received one report of a child putting the container over his mouth. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, The Children's Place Announce Recall of Shirts and Rompers
reason: The buttons can come off, posing a small parts choking hazard to young children.
distribution: The Children's Place stores nationwide sold the shirts and rompers, from January 2000 through July 2000. The shirts cost about $12 and the rompers cost about $14.
hazards: The buttons can come off, posing a small parts choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these clothes away from their children immediately. Consumers should return the clothes to the nearest The Children's Place store for a full refund and a 10 percent discount coupon.
injuries: The Children's Place has received three reports of buttons detaching. No injuries have been reported.

title: Weather Radios Recalled by Oregon Scientific
reason: The radio can fail to decode certain signals broadcast by the National Weather Service or can provide incorrect warnings of severe weather that puts lives and property at risk.
firm: Oregon Scientific Inc., of Tualatin, Ore.
distribution: Office super stores, mass merchandise, home and hardware stores, catalog, and websites sold the radios, from December 1999 through July 2000, for about $70.
hazards: The radio can fail to decode certain signals broadcast by the National Weather Service or can provide incorrect warnings of severe weather that puts lives and property at risk.
remedies: Consumers should not rely on the recalled weather radios to receive emergency information. Call Oregon Scientific for instructions on returning the radio to receive a free replacement. Oregon Scientific will reimburse consumers for postage.
injuries: The firm has received 12 reports from consumers that did not receive an emergency signal broadcast by the National Weather Service. No injuries have been reported.

title: Gel Pens Recalled by Colorbök
product: Gel pens included with Icee Black notebooks and Icee Black notepads
reason: Because these pens contain an extra spring, the end caps can shoot off with great force, posing a risk of eye and facial injuries.
firm: Colorbök, of Dexter, Mich.
distribution: Department, drug, grocery, and toy stores sold the notebooks and notepads with these pens, from June 2000 through July 2000, for about $5.
hazards: Because these pens contain an extra spring, the end caps can shoot off with great force, posing a risk of eye and facial injuries.
remedies: Stop using these gel pens immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a replacement pen.
injuries: None reported

title: CPSC, Kids Line Inc. Announce Recall to Repair "Le Cradle" Bassinets
reason: Infants can become entrapped in an opening between the bassinet's side and mattress platform and suffocate. Additionally, fabric can separate from the metal frame. Infants can be injured when they scrape against or become caught in the frame.
firm: Kids Line Inc., of Los Angeles, Calif.
distribution: Children's products stores nationwide sold the bassinets, from January 1989 through May 2000, for between $100 and $200.
hazards: Infants can become entrapped in an opening between the bassinet's side and mattress platform and suffocate. Additionally, fabric can separate from the metal frame. Infants can be injured when they scrape against or become caught in the frame.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the bassinets immediately and contact Kids Line for a free in-home repair kit, designed to secure the fabric around the bassinet, to prevent entrapments and exposure to the metal frame.
injuries: Kids Line has received one report of a 3-month-old boy in Oakland Park, Fla. who died when he suffocated after becoming trapped between the bassinet's side and mattress platform. Three other infants were scraped and bruised from contact with the metal frame that became exposed when the fabric separated from the frame.

title: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Swings and Toys
product: Fisher-Price "Lift & Lock Swings" and "Get Up & Go Walkers"
reason: Life & Lock Swings: Children can maneuver out of the restraints and fall out of the swings, resulting in serious injuries. Get Up & Go Walkers: Young children leaning forward on the front of the toys can tip them over and fall. Also, the windshield wipers on some of the toys, which stick out, can injure young children when they fall.
firm: Fisher-Price, of East Aurora, N.Y.
distribution: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount department stores sold the Lift & Lock Swings, from January 1991 through August 2000, for about $19. Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores sold the Get Up & Go Walkers, from July 1997 through August 2000, for about $30.
hazards: Life & Lock Swings: Children can maneuver out of the restraints and fall out of the swings, resulting in serious injuries. Get Up & Go Walkers: Young children leaning forward on the front of the toys can tip them over and fall. Also, the windshield wipers on some of the toys, which stick out, can injure young children when they fall.
remedies: Life & Lock Swings: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately. Fisher-Price will provide a free repair kit with a supplemental waist and crotch restraint belt.g et Up & Go Walkers: Consumers should stop children from using the toys immediately and call Fisher-Price for a free repair kit that will eliminate the front bar and windshield wiper.
injuries: Lift & Lock Swings: Eight children suffered serious injuries, including a fractured skull, leg, arm and two collarbones; two concussions; and stitches to the forehead. Thirty children received minor injuries including bumps, bruises and scrapes. Get Up & Go Walkers: Fisher-Price has received 330 reports of children falling while using or near the product. A total of 132 children received injuries such as bumps, bruises, scratches and cuts.

title: Swivel Rocker Chairs Recalled by Tropitone Furniture
reason: The base of the chair can crack, causing the person seated in the chair to fall.
firm: Tropitone Furniture Co., of Irvine, Calif.
distribution: Outdoor/patio furniture stores nationwide sold the chairs, from January 2000 through May 2000, for between $250 and $280.
hazards: The base of the chair can crack, causing the person seated in the chair to fall.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the swivel rocker chairs and contact Tropitone Furniture Co. to receive a free replacement base for their rocker chair.
injuries: Tropitone has received five reports of the base of these chairs cracking, and one report of a consumer falling from a chair. No injuries have been reported.

title: Girl's Nightshirts Recalled by the William Carter Co.
reason: The nightshirts, which fail to meet federal children's sleepwear flammability standards, could ignite easily and present a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
firm: The William Carter Co. (Carter's), of Morrow, Ga.
distribution: Carter's, department and specialty stores sold these pajamas nationwide, from May 2000 through August 2000, for between $10 and $13.
hazards: The nightshirts, which fail to meet federal children's sleepwear flammability standards, could ignite easily and present a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.
remedies: Take these nightshirts away from children immediately, and call Carter's for instructions on returning the nightshirts for a refund and a $15 Carter's gift certificate.

title: CPSC, The Penray Companies Inc. Announce Recall of Starting Fluid
product: Penray, Super-X, and Service Pro cans of starting fluid
reason: The starting fluid is extremely flammable and the leaking fluid poses a fire hazard. Direct contact with the product also can irritate the consumer's eyes and skin.
firm: The Penray Companies Inc., of Wheeling, Ill.
distribution: Automobile repair and rebuild shops sold the starting fluid nationwide, from November 1999 through August 2000, for $2 to $3.
hazards: The starting fluid is extremely flammable and the leaking fluid poses a fire hazard. Direct contact with the product also can irritate the consumer's eyes and skin.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled starting fluid immediately. Place it in a well-ventilated area away from sparks or flames. Consumers should call Penray for information on how to dispose of these cans, and how to get a refund.
injuries: Penray has received three reports of cans of the starting fluid leaking. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Playskool Announce Recall to Replace Busy Poppin' Pals Toys
reason: Small springs inside the toy can break loose, posing a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
distribution: Mass merchandise and toy stores, including Toys R Us, sold these toys nationwide for about $10. The toys were sold from January 1996 through August 2000.
hazards: Small springs inside the toy can break loose, posing a choking and laceration hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and contact Playskool to receive a free, redesigned replacement toy.
injuries: Playskool has received 16 reports of the springs breaking. Five children put the broken springs in their mouths, resulting in two children suffering lacerations.

title: CPSC, Manco Products Inc. Announce Recall to Repair of Go-Karts
product: Go-karts sold under the Manco, Phoenix, Fox, Rattler and Coyote labels
reason: These go-karts have guards designed to help prevent entanglements, but riders' long hair or loose clothing still can become entangled in partially exposed rotating components behind the drivers' seats, causing death or serious injury.
firm: Manco Products Inc., of Fort Wayne, Ind.
distribution: Outdoor power equipment dealers; specialty, discount, hardware, automotive parts supply and agricultural supply stores; and motorcycle dealers sold the go-karts nationwide, from January 1983 through July 2000, for between $600 and $2,000.
hazards: These go-karts have guards designed to help prevent entanglements, but riders' long hair or loose clothing still can become entangled in partially exposed rotating components behind the drivers' seats, causing death or serious injury.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these go-karts immediately and call Manco for a free repair kit with instructions for easy installation. Consumers also can contact any Manco dealer to get free installation of the repair kit.
injuries: Manco Products has received a report of one death and two reports of serious injuries when teenage girls' long hair became entangled in the rotating components. It was reported that a 13-year-old girl from Idaho, died from a fractured neck when her hair got caught in the drive chain and sprocket of a go-kart she was driving. Another 13-year-old girl suffered a scalping injury, and a 16-year-old girl lost consciousness and suffered severe head trauma.

title: CPSC, Williams-Sonoma Inc. Announce Recall of Portable Gas Grills
reason: The grills can be difficult or impossible to turn off and the temperature control can malfunction. This poses fire, burn, and explosion hazards to consumers.
distribution: Williams-Sonoma stores, in addition to the Williams-Sonoma catalog and website, sold the grills nationwide, from March 2000 through July 2000, for about $200.
hazards: The grills can be difficult or impossible to turn off and the temperature control can malfunction. This poses fire, burn, and explosion hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the grills immediately, and return them to Williams-Sonoma for a full refund and a $50 gift certificate. The firm will reimburse consumers for shipping, and will retrieve the grills from consumers' homes, upon request.
injuries: Williams-Sonoma and CPSC have received two reports of consumers being unable to shut off the propane gas flow. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, KFC Corporation Announce Recall of Toy Included With KFC Kids Meals
product: Tangled Treeples toys included with KFC Kids Meals
reason: The bottom of the container can fit over a child's nose and mouth, which could pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age.
distribution: KFC restaurants nationwide included the Tangled Treeples toys with KFC Kids Meals from June 2000 through July 2000.
hazards: The bottom of the container can fit over a child's nose and mouth, which could pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the green plastic container away from children under the age of three. They should discard the container or return it to any KFC restaurant for an individual-sized side item, such as macaroni and cheese.
injuries: A 19-month-old girl reportedly had the Tangled Treeples container stuck over her face, causing her distress. When her mother removed the container, there was a red mark left on the child's face.

title: CPSC, Polaris Industries Inc. Announce Recall of All-Terrain Vehicles
reason: The throttles on these ATVs can stick, preventing the ATV from slowing down when released. This can cause the vehicle to lose control and crash, resulting in severe injury or death.
firm: Polaris Industries Inc., of Minneapolis, Minn.
distribution: Polaris ATV dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from December 1998 through July 2000 ,for between $4,800 and $5,900.
hazards: The throttles on these ATVs can stick, preventing the ATV from slowing down when released. This can cause the vehicle to lose control and crash, resulting in severe injury or death.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these ATVs immediately. Registered owners of the recalled Polaris ATVs were notified by mail about the recall, and also will be contacted by their dealer to schedule a free ATV repair. Consumers should contact their local ATV dealer to get more information about the recall.
injuries: Polaris has received 26 reports of problems with the throttles on these ATVs. There have been 17 reports of crashes, resulting in six consumers suffering injuries.

title: CPSC, Minoura Announce Recall of Bicycle Indoor Training Stands
reason: These stands allow regular bicycles to be used as stationary bicycles. The flywheels, which are red or blue, can fracture in use. Metal pieces of broken flywheels can hit riders or bystanders, causing cuts and bruises.
firm: Minoura Company Ltd., of Japan
distribution: Bicycle stores and catalogs, including Performance, sold the stands nationwide, from January 1989 through December 1994, for between $120 and $180.
hazards: These stands allow regular bicycles to be used as stationary bicycles. The flywheels, which are red or blue, can fracture in use. Metal pieces of broken flywheels can hit riders or bystanders, causing cuts and bruises.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these stands immediately, and call Minoura, to receive a free repair kit.
injuries: Minoura has received three reports of injuries from pieces of broken flywheels, resulting in lacerations on riders' legs.

title: CPSC, Safety 1st Announce Recall to Repair Baby Walkers
reason: Babies can lose their lower teeth when the teeth are caught in parts of the three-spoke steering wheels. Also, on some of these walkers, the telephone could break apart, releasing small parts and posing a choking hazard.
firm: Safety 1st Inc., of Canton, Mass.
distribution: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount department stores nationwide sold the walkers, from April 1998 through April 1999, for about $50.
hazards: Babies can lose their lower teeth when the teeth are caught in parts of the three-spoke steering wheels. Also, on some of these walkers, the telephone could break apart, releasing small parts and posing a choking hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these walkers immediately, and contact Safety 1st. Repair kit no longer available. New cash incentive is being offered or replacement product. Do not use these products. Please discard or destroy these products.
injuries: Safety 1st has received eight reports of babies catching their teeth in parts of the three-spoke steering wheels. Six babies lost lower front teeth. There also are 44 reports of the telephone button loosening. One 6-month-old baby girl gagged on a telephone button from a phone that came apart.

title: CPSC, Kmart Announce Recall of Children's Swim Masks
reason: The mask's glass lens can break into sharp pieces, causing lacerations to a child's face, eyes or hands.
distribution: Kmart and Super Kmart stores nationwide sold the swim masks, from February 2000 to July 2000, for about $3.
hazards: The mask's glass lens can break into sharp pieces, causing lacerations to a child's face, eyes or hands.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these swim masks immediately and return them to the nearest Kmart or Super Kmart store for a refund.
injuries: Kmart has received one report of the glass lens shattering. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Appliance Co. of America LLC Announce Recall of Juice Extractors Sold at Kmart
reason: The juice extractor's filter and lid can break apart, and project metal and plastic into the air, causing injuries to nearby consumers.
firm: Appliance Co. of American LLC, of Great Neck, N.Y.
distribution: Kmart stores nationwide sold these juice extractors, from September 1992 through June 1995, for about $21.
hazards: The juice extractor's filter and lid can break apart, and project metal and plastic into the air, causing injuries to nearby consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these juice extractors immediately, and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and cannot be contacted, and a remedy is no longer available.
injuries: Appliance Co. of America had received 17 reports of the juice extractors' filters and lids breaking apart. Six consumers suffered minor cuts to their hands and arms.

title: CPSC, Rashti & Rashti Announce Recall of Pacifier Clips
product: Magic Years® Novelty Pacifier Buddy Clips
reason: The metal clip and the small rivet that attaches the clip to a small, stuffed animal on the pacifier holder can break apart easily, exposing babies to small parts. This poses a choking and aspiration hazard to babies.
distribution: Gift and specialty stores sold the pacifier clips, from September 1999 through June 2000. The pacifier clips sold individually for about $3, and the bib/pacifier clip sets sold for about $5.
hazards: The metal clip and the small rivet that attaches the clip to a small, stuffed animal on the pacifier holder can break apart easily, exposing babies to small parts. This poses a choking and aspiration hazard to babies.
remedies: Consumers should take these pacifier clips away from babies immediately, and call Rashti & Rashti for information on receiving a refund.
injuries: Rashti & Rashti received one report of a pacifier clip breaking apart. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC and The Coleman Co. Announce Recall of Gas Grills
reason: A sharp edge on the metal heat shield below the control panel of the grill can cause lacerations to the hands, wrists or arms.
firm: The Coleman Co. of Witchita, Kan.
distribution: Home improvement and discount department stores sold the grills nationwide from January through April 2000 for between $350 and $500.
hazards: A sharp edge on the metal heat shield below the control panel of the grill can cause lacerations to the hands, wrists or arms.
remedies: Consumers should immediately contact Coleman to receive a free repair kit. The repair kit contains a plastic sheath to cover the sharp edge on the heat shield.
injuries: Coleman has received six reports from consumers who received cuts or lacerations on their hands, wrists, or arms from the heat shield when they were accessing the propane cylinder underneath the grill.

title: CPSC, AmeriGas Propane L.P. Announce Recall of Propane Cylinders
reason: Of these cylinders, about 10 could be overfilled, which can cause them to release flammable propane gas unexpectedly, posing a risk of fires and explosions.
firm: AmeriGas Propane L.P., of Valley Forge, Pa.
distribution: Home Depots and Meijer's stores in the Detroit, Mich., area sold or exchanged these propane cylinders on July 17 through July 19. The cylinders sold for between $44 and $48 and cost between $13 and $14 for an exchange.
hazards: Of these cylinders, about 10 could be overfilled, which can cause them to release flammable propane gas unexpectedly, posing a risk of fires and explosions.
remedies: Consumers who purchased or exchanged one of these AmeriGas barbecue propane cylinders should not use their gas grills or other appliances, and should not disconnect or transport the cylinder. Consumers should call the AmeriGas for instructions on getting their gas cylinder inspected and replaced, if needed.
injuries: On July 19, 2000, some of the overfilled cylinders vented propane and ignited, causing an explosion at the AmeriGas plant in Willoughby, Ohio. One worker suffered minor burns. No consumer injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Hufco-Delaware Co. Announce Recall to Repair Gerry® TrailTech™ Backpack Baby Carriers
product: Gerry® TrailTech™ backpack baby carriers with plastic frames
reason: Small infants can shift to one side, slip through the leg openings of these carriers and fall.
firm: Hufco-Delaware Co., of Miamisburg, Ohio
distribution: Department and baby products stores nationwide sold these backpack carriers, from January 1996 through July 2000, for about $65.
hazards: Small infants can shift to one side, slip through the leg openings of these carriers and fall.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these backpack carriers immediately. Evenflo, which is now the responding company for this recall, no longer has any service parts for this product nor the capability of producing these parts. As repair kits are no longer available, consumers should destroy these products.
injuries: CPSC and Hufco-Delaware have received four reports of infants slipping through the leg openings of these carriers. There were two reports of infants suffering fractured skulls and two reports of infants suffering bumped heads when they fell to the ground.

title: CPSC, Master Lock Co. Announce Recall to Replace Gun Locks
reason: Due to a manufacturing discrepancy, the two halves of some gun locks can be manually separated without a key, giving children and others unauthorized access to a firearm.
firm: Master Lock Co., of Milwaukee, Wis.
distribution: Stores, such as Walmart, Kmart, Gander Mountain and Sports Authority, sold the gun locks nationwide, between June 1999 and July 2000, for between $8 and $12.
hazards: Due to a manufacturing discrepancy, the two halves of some gun locks can be manually separated without a key, giving children and others unauthorized access to a firearm.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled locks immediately and call Master Lock to receive a free replacement lock. As always, consumers are reminded not to use gun locks on loaded guns. Until the replacement lock is received, consumers should not use the recalled gun locks. Master Lock urges consumers to comply with all state and local laws requiring the use of gun locking devices.
injuries: Master Lock reports it has not received any consumer reports of locks being disabled as a result of this discrepancy. This recall is being conducted by Master Lock to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Gymboree Announce Recall of Plush Shape Sorters and Stacking Toys
product: Plush Shape Sorter Toys and Plush Stacking Toys
reason: The stuffing of the toys can contain sewing needles and sharp metal pieces. Young children could ingest or be cut by these sharp metal pieces.
distribution: Gymboree and Play & Music Stores, and the Gymboree web site sold the toys nationwide from November 1998 through April 2000 for about $20.
hazards: The stuffing of the toys can contain sewing needles and sharp metal pieces. Young children could ingest or be cut by these sharp metal pieces.
remedies: Stop using the toys immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
injuries: There has been one report of a part of a sewing needle in the stuffing of the plush shape sorter toy. After searching through its inventory, the firm found five additional plush shape sorter toys with sharp metal pieces. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Shelcore Inc. Announce Recall Children's Play Tables to Replace Mallets
reason: The mallet that comes as part of this table set can be lodged into the throats of young children, posing a choking hazard.
firm: Shelcore Inc., of Somerset, N.J.
distribution: Toy stores nationwide sold these play tables, from March 1996 through March 1999, for between $18 and $20.
hazards: The mallet that comes as part of this table set can be lodged into the throats of young children, posing a choking hazard.
remedies: Consumers should immediately throw the recalled mallets in the trash, and call Shelcore for a free replacement mallet.
injuries: Shelcore received a report of the mallet being jammed into the throat of a 13-month old boy after he fell while teething on the ball end of the mallet. Lacerations in the throat resulted when an adult had to forcibly remove the mallet, to prevent choking.

title: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Baby Jumper Seats and Construction Toys
product: "Hop, Skip, Jumper" activity seats and Big Action Construction Toys
reason: The spring that suspends the jumper seat from the doorway can break. Babies can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries. The crane of the construction toy has a bucket that is attached by a 25-inch strap. The bucket can be raised and lowered by using a turning crank on the crane. Children can wrap the 25-inch strap around their necks, posing a strangulation hazard.
firm: Fisher-Price, of East Aurora, N.Y.
distribution: Hop, Skip, Jumpers: The Hop, Skip, Jumpers were sold by mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount stores, from January 1987 through January 1994, for about $25.Construction toys: Toy, mass merchandise and discount stores sold the Big Action Construction toys nationwide, from January 1997 through June 2000, for about $60.
hazards: The spring that suspends the jumper seat from the doorway can break. Babies can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries. The crane of the construction toy has a bucket that is attached by a 25-inch strap. The bucket can be raised and lowered by using a turning crank on the crane. Children can wrap the 25-inch strap around their necks, posing a strangulation hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the jumpers immediately. Fisher-Price will provide a free repair kit with a new, suspension strap to support the jumper seat if the spring breaks. The repair can be done quickly and easily in the home. Consumers should cut the 25-inch strap off of the construction toy immediately and throw the strap away. Fisher-Price will provide a free replacement crane boom and bucket with a 12-inch strap so that children cannot wrap it around their necks.
injuries: Hop, Skip, Jumpers: Fisher-Price has received 80 reports of the springs breaking. Twenty babies have been injured. The injuries include nine lacerations to heads, five of which required stitches or staples, a dislocated tailbone, a black eye and bumps, bruises and scrapes. Construction toys: Fisher-Price has received 16 reports of children wrapping the strap around their necks. Seven children suffered minor injuries.

remedies: Parents and caregivers should take these toys away from young children immediately. Consumers should send the toy back to the firm to receive another toy of similar value. The firm will pay postage costs.
injuries: CPSC has received one report of a 5-month-old girl in El Paso, Texas, choking to death after one of the small balls attached to these toys lodged in her throat. CPSC also received reports of two children starting to choke on a ball from this toy.

title: Teethers Recalled by Manhattan Group LLC

title: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Doll Feeding Sets

title: CPSC, Burley Design Cooperative Announce Recall to Repair Burely-Bravo™ Bicycle Trailers

title: CPSC, Whitehall-Robins Healthcare Announce Recall of Teething Rings

hazards: When bent, these teething rings can fit into an infant's mouth and trigger a gagging reflex. This poses a risk of vomiting, which could result in choking and aspiration.
remedies: Consumers should take these teething rings away from infants immediately. Contact Whitehall-Robins Healthcare for information on returning the teething ring in order to receive a free Anbesol® product.
injuries: Whitehall-Robins Healthcare has received two reports from consumers of children gagging on the teething rings, including one report of a child starting to choke.

title: CPSC, Kellogg Company Announce Recall of Toy Cars Inside Boxes of Cereal
product: Kellogg's Nascar® Pull'N Go Hot Wheels
reason: The tires can detach from the wheels of these cars, posing a choking hazard for young children.

hazards: The tires can detach from the wheels of these cars, posing a choking hazard for young children.

injuries: Kellogg has received two reports of the tires detaching from the wheels of these toy cars. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Today's Kids Announce Recall of Spinning Ride Toys

hazards: The center column can break, causing a child to suddenly fall backward or be hit in the face by the broken column.

title: CPSC, Galoob Toys Inc. Announce Recall of Sky Dancers® Flying Dolls
reason: The hard plastic Sky Dancers® dolls can fly rapidly in unpredictable directions, and can hit and injure both children and adults.

hazards: The hard plastic Sky Dancers® dolls can fly rapidly in unpredictable directions, and can hit and injure both children and adults.

They include eye injuries, including scratched corneas and incidents of temporary blindness, broken teeth, a mild concussion, a broken rib, and facial lacerations that required stitches.

title: CPSC, Apollo Presentation Products Announce Recall of Light Boxes
reason: The light boxes have loose wires and lack adequate grounding, presenting fire, electrocution and shock hazards to consumers.

hazards: The light boxes have loose wires and lack adequate grounding, presenting fire, electrocution and shock hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled light boxes immediately, and call ACCO Brands Customer Care (which is now handling this recall) for instructions on returning the projectors to the company, for a refund.
injuries: CPSC has received two reports of loose wires, one in which the light box caught fire, resulting in $5,000 property damage. No injuries have been reported.

remedies: Consumers with a recalled hedge trimmer or auger should stop using it immediately and return it to any authorized Tanaka service dealer for a free repair. The equipment will be fitted with a redesigned fuel tank.
injuries: Tanaka and CPSC have received one report of a hedge trimmer catching fire and causing minor damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Vtech Industries Announce Recall of Toy Baby Phone

injuries: Jetmax has received five reports of these chairs collapsing and children falling. One 13-month-old girl suffered a laceration requiring 18 stitches.

Consumers should send the pacifiers to Playtex Pacifiers, Playtex Products Inc., 20 Troy Road, Whippany, NJ 07981. Playtex will reimburse consumers for postage.
injuries: Playtex has received 21 reports of pacifier nipples detaching from the shields. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Ace Hardware Corp. Announce Recall of Vinyl Window Blinds
reason: These blinds contain lead exceeding government guidelines, and do not have required labeling warning they contain lead. Over time, vinyl deteriorates from exposure to sunlight and heat, forming lead dust on the surface of the blind. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
distribution: Ace Hardware and other hardware stores nationwide sold the window blinds, from August 1999 through May 2000, for between $6 and $27.
hazards: These blinds contain lead exceeding government guidelines, and do not have required labeling warning they contain lead. Over time, vinyl deteriorates from exposure to sunlight and heat, forming lead dust on the surface of the blind. Young children can ingest lead by wiping their hands on the blinds and then putting their hands in their mouths. Lead poisoning in children is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.
remedies: Consumers should remove the window blinds from windows and keep them away from children. Consumers can return the window blinds to the store where they were purchased, for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and Ace Hardware are not aware of any lead poisonings involving these window blinds. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of lead poisonings.

distribution: These robes were sold at Bloomingdale's, Burdines, Goldsmith's, Lazarus, Macy's, Rich's, and The Bon Marché, from July 1995 through January 2000, for about $25 to $52.
hazards: These robes, when used as sleepwear, fail to meet federal flammability standards for children's sleepwear. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burn injuries to children.
remedies: Parents should immediately stop their children from wearing these robes and return the robes to the store where purchased, for a full refund.
injuries: Federated Department Stores has not received any reports of injuries from these robes. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Warner Bros. Studio Store Announce Recall of Tweety Rattles and Sandals

title: CPSC, Jack Rabbit Creations Recall Wooden Stacking Toys
