title: CPSC, By Us International Co. Ltd. Announce Recall of Bicycle Components
product: Ballistic front suspension forks installed on Mongoose S-20 and MGX S-20 bicycles
reason: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control and fall.
firm: By Us International Co. Ltd., of Taiwan
distribution: Discount department and toy stores nationwide sold these bicycles, from September 1998 through May 2000, for between $125 and $150.
hazards: The forks on these bicycles can break apart, causing riders to lose control and fall.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these bicycles and call Brunswick Bicycles for information on receiving a free replacement fork, including installation.
injuries: By Us and Brunswick have received 18 reports of forks on these bicycles breaking, resulting in nine riders, including teenagers, suffering serious head and bodily injuries, abrasions, bruises and chipped teeth.

title: CPSC, Answer Products Inc. Announce Recall of Bicycle Components
product: Answer and Manitou brand bicycle forks
reason: The tube that attaches the fork to the bicycle can fail, causing riders to lose control and fall.
firm: Answer Products Inc., of Valencia, Calif.
distribution: Bicycle stores nationwide and mail order catalogs sold these forks and bikes from August 1999 through May 2000. The forks range in price from $245 to $695, and the assembled bicycles with these forks range in price from $1,200 to more than $3,000.
hazards: The tube that attaches the fork to the bicycle can fail, causing riders to lose control and fall.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop riding the bicycles with these forks and take them to an authorized Answer Products dealer, for a free inspection and repair.
injuries: Answer Products has received six reports of these forks failing, resulting in two consumers suffering minor injuries, including cuts, bruises and chipped teeth.

title: CPSC, Weed Wizard Acquisition Corp. Announce Recall of Weed Trimmer Heads With Metal Chains
reason: The end link of the trimmer's metal chain can rapidly and unexpectedly detach during use, propelling the link into the air at a high velocity. If the metal link strikes the user or a bystander, it can penetrate skin and bone, causing injury or death.
firm: Weed Wizard Acquisition Corp., of Bradley, Mich.
distribution: Home centers, mass merchants, discount stores, hardware stores and television advertisements nationwide sold Weed Wizards with metal chains, from May 1987 through April 2000, for between $19 and $25. The replacement chain kits were sold from January 1992 through April 2000 for about $8.
hazards: The end link of the trimmer's metal chain can rapidly and unexpectedly detach during use, propelling the link into the air at a high velocity. If the metal link strikes the user or a bystander, it can penetrate skin and bone, causing injury or death.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the Weed Wizards with metal chains immediately and discard or destroy the product. The firm is out of business and a remedy is no longer available. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
injuries: Weed Wizard and CPSC have received 47 reports of metal links detaching from trimmers, resulting in 41 injuries, including the death of a 3-year-old girl in Alabama, who was struck in the head by a metal link. The injuries included users and bystanders being struck by metal links in the head, neck, legs, ankles and feet, resulting in penetration wounds and lacerations.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Jogging Strollers
product: BOB Sport Utility Stroller and BOB Sport Utility Stroller D'lux jogging strollers
reason: The stroller's front wheel connector can crack during use, causing the wheel to separate from the frame. A jogger could lose control of the stroller, or the stroller could suddenly collapse, resulting in injury to a child.
firm: BOB Trailers Inc., of San Luis Obispo, Calif.
distribution: Bike, baby and outdoor product stores and websites retailers sold the strollers nationwide, from November 1998 through March 2000, for about $280 to $370.
hazards: The stroller's front wheel connector can crack during use, causing the wheel to separate from the frame. A jogger could lose control of the stroller, or the stroller could suddenly collapse, resulting in injury to a child.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the stroller immediately, and return it to the store where purchased, for repair. Consumers also can return the strollers to BOB Trailers, for repair.
injuries: BOB Trailers has received seven reports of the wheel connector cracking, causing the front wheel to become loose. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Jogging Strollers
reason: Strollers were shipped without straps attached to the frame to secure the seat. Unless the frame straps are attached, a child in the seat of the stroller can lean forward and fall out.
firm: Baby Trend Inc., of Ontario, Calif.
distribution: Baby's "R" Us stores sold the strollers nationwide, between January 1999 and April 1999, for about $200.
hazards: Strollers were shipped without straps attached to the frame to secure the seat. Unless the frame straps are attached, a child in the seat of the stroller can lean forward and fall out.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these strollers immediately and examine the stroller, to determine if the seat is strapped to the stroller frame.
injuries: Baby Trend has received one report of an 8-month-old baby boy leaning forward in a stroller with unsecured seat straps, falling out of the seat and bumping his head.

title: CPSC, Healthtex Announce Recall of Baby Garments
product: Healthtex® and Little Impressions® baby garments
reason: Snaps on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to babies.
firm: Healthtex, a division of VF Playwear Inc., of Greensboro, N.C.
distribution: Department stores and children's specialty stores nationwide as well as the Healthtex website sold these clothes, from May 1999 through December 1999, for between $12 and $30.
hazards: Snaps on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to babies.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these baby garments immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a refund or exchange. Consumers also can return garments directly to the manufacturer.
injuries: CPSC and Healthtex have received 10 reports of snaps detaching from the baby garments. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Sta-Rite Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Battery Chargers
product: Battery chargers used in "Flotec" and "Sears" back-up sump pump systems
reason: The battery chargers can overheat and ignite, melting the charger housing and posing a fire hazard.
firm: Sta-Rite Industries Inc., of Delavan, Wis.
distribution: Large and small home centers, auto parts and plumbing supply stores, including Sears, W.W. Grainger, Advanced Auto Parts, Home Quarters, Home Depot, and Hechinger sold the sump pump systems nationwide, from December 1994 through September 1997, for about $200. The battery chargers also were sold as a replacement part for the sump pump systems for about $130.
hazards: The battery chargers can overheat and ignite, melting the charger housing and posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the sump pumps with the recalled battery charger immediately.
injuries: Sta-Rite has received seven reports of battery chargers overheating or catching fire. Four incidents have involved smoke or fire damage to homes, confined to the immediate area of the charger. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Children's Lamps
reason: The lamps can short circuit, posing a fire hazard.
firm: Kmart Corp., of Troy, Mich.
distribution: Kmart stores nationwide sold the lamps, from January 1993 through March 2000, for between $13 and $15.
hazards: The lamps can short circuit, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should immediately unplug the lamps and stop using them. Consumers should return the lamps to their local Kmart, for a refund.
injuries: Kmart has received eight reports of the lamps short circuiting and catching fire, resulting in property damage. One of these fires resulted in more than $15,000 in damages, and another caused more than $3,000 in damages. No injuries or deaths have been reported.

title: CPSC, Graco Announce Recall of Infant Swings
reason: The restraint systems on the older swings consist of a waist belt only and a hinged or removable tray, which serves as a restraint. If parts are missing, the restraints are not used, or the tray pops off, infants can slip down into the seat and strangle or fall from the swing.
firm: Graco Children's Products Inc., of Elverson, Pa.
distribution: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount stores nationwide sold the Graco swings through approximately January 1998, for between $70 to about $120.
hazards: The restraint systems on the older swings consist of a waist belt only and a hinged or removable tray, which serves as a restraint. If parts are missing, the restraints are not used, or the tray pops off, infants can slip down into the seat and strangle or fall from the swing.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately. To receive the free safety restraint, consumers should call Graco. Consumers should have the swing in front of them when they call so that Graco can determine if the swing needs the new safety restraint.
injuries: There have been six deaths. These occurred when parts were missing or the restraints were not used and infants slid down the swings' seats and became tangled in the restraints. In five instances, the swings were second-hand. Of 209 incidents, 181 were reports of infants falling from the swing. In nine of the falls, infants suffered serious injuries including bone fractures and concussions. Twenty-two infants were caught at the neck or chest.

title: CPSC, Proctor-Silex Announce Recall of Toasters
reason: The heating elements in these toasters can remain on after the toast pops up. This poses a fire hazard.
distribution: Mass merchandise stores nationwide, including Ames, Bradlees, Burdines, Eckerd, Rite Aid, Servistar and Walgreens, sold these toasters, from April 1997 through September 1999, for between $20 and $25.
hazards: The heating elements in these toasters can remain on after the toast pops up. This poses a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should immediately unplug and stop using these toasters. For information on receiving a free replacement toaster, consumers should call Proctor-Silex.
injuries: CPSC and Proctor-Silex have received at least 24 complaints from consumers of these toasters staying on after the toast popped up. There have been three reports of food fires, resulting in property damage to kitchen cabinets. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, John Deere Consumer Products Inc. Announce Recall of Homelite® Handheld Power Blowers/Vacuums
reason: The fuel line location can cause it to contact the edge of the engine shroud, causing the line to prematurely wear. This can result in a gasoline leak, presenting a fire hazard and causing burn injuries to consumers.
firm: John Deere Consumer Products Inc., of Charlotte, N.C.
distribution: Home center and hardware stores including the Home Depot, Eagle Hardware and Ace Hardware, sold these blowers/vacuums nationwide, from August 1998 through January 2000, for about $150.
hazards: The fuel line location can cause it to contact the edge of the engine shroud, causing the line to prematurely wear. This can result in a gasoline leak, presenting a fire hazard and causing burn injuries to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these power blowers/vacuums immediately and contact their nearest Homelite® service dealer for a free inspection and repair.
injuries: John Deere Consumer Products has received two reports of the fuel line leaking from these power blowers/vacuums. There have been no reports of fires or injuries.

title: CPSC, American Honda Motor Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Lawnmowers
reason: The lawnmowers' fuel tanks' seam can split or crack, leaking fuel, and creating a fire and burn hazard to consumers.
firm: American Honda Motor Co. Inc., of Torrance, Calif.
distribution: Honda power equipment dealers and The Home Depot sold the lawnmowers nationwide, from May 1998 through January 2000, for about $430.
hazards: The lawnmowers' fuel tanks' seam can split or crack, leaking fuel, and creating a fire and burn hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these lawnmowers immediately, and check to see if the gas tank is leaking. If there is a leak, immediately move the mower away from any possible ignition sources, for example, water heaters or electric appliances. Empty the fuel tank by following owner manual instructions. Consumers should take these mowers to a Honda power equipment dealer, who will inspect and replace the fuel tanks free of charge.
injuries: American Honda Motor Co. has 25 reports of fuel leaking from these lawnmowers. There have been no fires or injuries reported.

title: CPSC, Fisher-Price Announce Recall of Infant Products
product: 3-in-1 Cradle Swing with Detachable Carrier and Bounce 'n Play™ Activity Dome
reason: When the 3-in-1 Cradle Swing detachable seat is used as a carrier, the locks for the handle can unexpectedly release, causing the seat to flip forward. When this happens, infants can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries. The nylon bands that hold the surface level of the Bounce 'n Play Activity Dome can detach, allowing the surface to tilt. This can cause an infant to slide down against one end and be trapped in a position, bsing difficult to breathe, posing a suffocation hazard.
firm: Fisher-Price, of East Aurora, N.Y.
distribution: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and major discount stores sold the 3-in-1 Cradle Swings nationwide, from March 1997 through January 1999, for about $100 and the Bounce 'n Play Activity Domes nationwide, from December 1998 through March 2000, for about $50.
hazards: When the 3-in-1 Cradle Swing detachable seat is used as a carrier, the locks for the handle can unexpectedly release, causing the seat to flip forward. When this happens, infants can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries. The nylon bands that hold the surface level of the Bounce 'n Play Activity Dome can detach, allowing the surface to tilt. This can cause an infant to slide down against one end and be trapped in a position, bsing difficult to breathe, posing a suffocation hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the swing's seat as a carrier immediately. Fisher-Price will provide a free repair kit that will lock the carrier's handle in place. The repair can be done quickly and easily in the home. Consumers can continue to use the seat as intended as a cradle swing. Consumers should stop using the Bounce 'n Play Activity Dome immediately. Fisher-Price has discontinued distribution of the repair kit for this product. Consumers should discontinue use of the item immediately.
injuries: There have been 28 reports of the 3-in-1 Cradle Swing carrier's handle unexpectedly releasing when used as a carrier, resulting in injuries to 10 infants. The injuries include a skull fracture, bumps, bruises and scrapes to the head. According to the reports, some injuries occurred to infants who were restrained in the seat. There have been 28 reports of the nylon band of the Bounce 'n Play Activity Dome detaching and causing the play and nap surface to tilt. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Toymax Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Skeet Shoot Game Cartridges
reason: The Skeet Shoot games' cartridges can be defective, and can cause the projector to overheat, melt and smoke, presenting a risk of burns to consumers.
distribution: Toy and discount department stores nationwide, including Toys R Us, Sam's Club, KB Toys™ and Costco, sold these games, from October 1998 through March 2000 ,for about $65.
hazards: The Skeet Shoot games' cartridges can be defective, and can cause the projector to overheat, melt and smoke, presenting a risk of burns to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these games immediately and remove the game cartridge from the console. To receive a free replacement game cartridge, or for more information, contact JAKKS Pacific, Inc. Consumers should not return these games or cartridges to stores.
injuries: Toymax has received 100 reports of projectors overheating, melting and smoking. A consumer reportedly suffering a minor burn injury on the hand, and damages included two scorched carpets and one scorched bedspread.

title: CPSC, BISSELL® Homecare Inc. Announce Recall of Upright Vacuum Cleaners
product: Bissel PowerClean™ and PureAir™ vacuum cleaners
reason: The power cord insulation can tear where the cord attaches to the vacuum, exposing bare wires. This poses a risk of shock and burns to consumers.
firm: BISSELL® Homecare Inc. of Grand Rapids, Mich.
distribution: Major discount, appliance and department stores sold these vacuum cleaners nationwide, from July 1998 through March 2000, for between $89 and $159.
hazards: The power cord insulation can tear where the cord attaches to the vacuum, exposing bare wires. This poses a risk of shock and burns to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these vacuum cleaners immediately, and contact BISSELL to arrange for a free repair through BISSELL's authorized service network. Vacuums cannot be repaired by the retailers.
injuries: BISSELL is aware of 54 reports of the cords on these vacuums tearing. There has been one report of a consumer suffering a burn injury on her hand.

title: Converters Recalled by Coast Electronics Supply
reason: The product presents an electrical shock hazard because the unplugged end of the cord is energized when the other end is plugged in.
distribution: Small electronic stores in California, Colorado, Missouri, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon and Texas sold the product for $25 to $30.
hazards: The product presents an electrical shock hazard because the unplugged end of the cord is energized when the other end is plugged in.
remedies: Stop using the product immediately and return it to the store where purchased, for a full refund.
injuries: A 4-year-old boy was shocked when he grasped the end of the cord.

title: Chairs Recalled by Boston Warehouse Trading Corp.
reason: The screws holding the chair's front leg folding mechanism can work loose, causing the chair to collapse, resulting in injury.
distribution: Specialty gift, department and furniture stores nationwide sold the chairs, from January 1999 through January 2000, for about $150.
hazards: The screws holding the chair's front leg folding mechanism can work loose, causing the chair to collapse, resulting in injury.
remedies: Stop using the chair immediately and contact Boston Warehouse Trading Corp. Consumers will be given the option of receiving replacement screws or returning the chair to the store where purchased, for a full refund.
injuries: Boston Warehouse Trading Corp. has received three reports of chairs collapsing, resulting in one muscle strain injury and one property damage incident.

title: CPSC, The Standard Mattress Co. Announce Futon Recall
reason: Some of these futons may fail cigarette ignition resistance tests, in violation of the federal Flammable Fabrics Act, because the boric acid flame retardant inside the futons may not have been evenly disbursed. This could result in burn injuries, should one of these futons catch fire.
firm: The Standard Mattress Co., of Hartford, Conn.
distribution: Furniture and futon stores nationwide sold the futons, from May 1998 through October 1998, for $140 to $250.
hazards: Some of these futons may fail cigarette ignition resistance tests, in violation of the federal Flammable Fabrics Act, because the boric acid flame retardant inside the futons may not have been evenly disbursed. This could result in burn injuries, should one of these futons catch fire.
remedies: Consumers who purchased one of these futons during this period should immediately call The Standard Mattress Co. to obtain a free replacement futon. Consumers should not return the futons to the stores where they purchased them. Replacements are available only by calling the company.
injuries: CPSC and The Standard Mattress Co. are not aware of any fires or injuries involving these futons. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Advance Thermo Control Announce Recall of Baby Wipe Warmers
reason: Cracks in the interior tub of these wipe warmers can allow water to contact the electrical components. This can result in consumers receiving an electric shock.
firm: Advance Thermo Control (ATC), of Hong Kong
distribution: Toy, department and baby specialty stores, including Toys "R" Us and Burlington Coat Factory, and mail order catalogs, sold these wipe warmers nationwide, from February 1998 through December 1999, for about $25.
hazards: Cracks in the interior tub of these wipe warmers can allow water to contact the electrical components. This can result in consumers receiving an electric shock.
remedies: Consumers should immediately unplug the warmers, remove the wipes, and check to see if the interior tub is cracked. If so, stop using the warmer immediately, and call ATC for information on receiving a free replacement unit. If the tub of the wipe warmer is not cracked, the unit is not part of the recall, and consumers can continue to use the appliance.
injuries: Prince Lionheart has received four reports of electric shocks when consumers touched the wipes in the warmers with cracked tubs.

title: CPSC, Russ Berrie & Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Rattles
reason: The shape and size of the rattle's handle allow it to become lodged in the throats of babies, posing a choking hazard. The rattles violate the Federal Hazardous Substances Act for the design and construction of baby rattles.
firm: Russ Berrie & Co. Inc., of Oakland, N.J
distribution: Specialty and drug stores, and flower and gift shops nationwide sold these rattles, from November 1998 through December 1999, for about $14.
hazards: The shape and size of the rattle's handle allow it to become lodged in the throats of babies, posing a choking hazard. The rattles violate the Federal Hazardous Substances Act for the design and construction of baby rattles.
remedies: Consumers should take these rattles away from babies immediately, and return them to the store where purchased, for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and Russ Berrie are not aware of any incidents or injuries involving these rattles.

title: CPSC, Ace Hardware Corp. Announce Recall of Shingling Hatchets
reason: The heads on these tools can detach when in use, striking the user or a bystander and causing serious injury.
distribution: Ace Hardware Stores nationwide sold the hatchet,s from March 1994 through April 2000, for about $18.
hazards: The heads on these tools can detach when in use, striking the user or a bystander and causing serious injury.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the hatchets immediately and return them to any Ace Hardware Store, for a refund.
injuries: Ace Hardware Corp. has received two reports of hatchet heads detaching, one of which struck a bystander in the head, resulting in a cut requiring 32 stitches.

title: CPSC, Maxim Enterprise Inc. and Zany Brainy Inc. Announce Recall of Wooden Pull Toy
reason: The pull toy's wheels can break off and the bead can detach from the pull string, posing small parts choking hazards to young children.
firm: Maxim Enterprise Inc., of Middleboro, Mass.
hazards: The pull toy's wheels can break off and the bead can detach from the pull string, posing small parts choking hazards to young children.
remedies: No remedy available.
injuries: The firms have received a report of wheels coming off and a report of the bead detaching from the pull string. The detached bead was found in a child's mouth. No injuries were reported.

title: CPSC, InSTEP™ LLC Announce Recall of Jogging Strollers
product: InSTEP and HEALTHRIDER single and double jogging strollers
reason: The stroller's brake can fail, causing the stroller to unexpectedly roll away, resulting in injury to a child.
firm: InSTEP™ LLC, of Mendota Heights, Minn.
distribution: Burlington Coat Factory, J.C. Penney, Healthrider, The Sports Authority and Target stores nationwide, among others, sold the strollers, from December 1998 through July 1999, for about $100 for a single jogger and $250 for a double jogger.
hazards: The stroller's brake can fail, causing the stroller to unexpectedly roll away, resulting in injury to a child.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the strollers immediately and contact InSTEP LLC to receive a free, easy-to-install repair kit.
injuries: InSTEP LLC has received five reports of brakes failing. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC Warns Against Baby Mattresses, Pads That Make Unfounded Claims About Reducing SIDS
reason: CPSC is warning consumers that certain baby mattresses and mattress pads encourage the potentially deadly practice of placing babies to sleep on their stomachs, and claim that the products reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS). Despite the claims, CPSC is not aware of any evidence that proves that babies can safely be placed to sleep on their stomachs on these products, or that using the products will reduce the risk of SIDS.
firm: Kid Safe, of Van Nuys, Calif.; U.S. Family Products, of Willard, Mo.; Sleep Guardian, of Charleston, S.C.; Jupiter Industries, of Ontario, Canada
distribution: The four products involved in CPSC's action have been sold for about $30 to $100 in baby, drug and discount department stores; in catalogs; and on the Internet, including the following web sites: www.sidsprevent.com, www.kidsafeprod.com and flashmall.com.
hazards: CPSC is warning consumers that certain baby mattresses and mattress pads encourage the potentially deadly practice of placing babies to sleep on their stomachs, and claim that the products reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS). Despite the claims, CPSC is not aware of any evidence that proves that babies can safely be placed to sleep on their stomachs on these products, or that using the products will reduce the risk of SIDS.
remedies: According to CPSC, the risk of SIDS is significantly reduced by placing babies to sleep on their backs in a crib that meets current safety standards and has a firm, tight-fitting mattress and no soft bedding.
injuries: There are about 3,000 Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) deaths per year - a reduction of about 38 percent in the 5 years following the American Academy of Pediatrics recommendation that babies be placed to sleep on their backs.

title: CPSC, Michael's Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Lighters
reason: These lighters can leak butane when they are ignited, causing an excessive burst of flame from the tip or other areas of the lighter. This presents a risk of fire and burn injuries to consumers.
hazards: These lighters can leak butane when they are ignited, causing an excessive burst of flame from the tip or other areas of the lighter. This presents a risk of fire and burn injuries to consumers.
remedies: No remedy available.
injuries: Michael's Stores Inc. has received 14 reports of excessive flame, resulting in three reports of burns to consumers' hands.

title: CPSC, Tim Hortons Announce Recall of Coffeemakers
reason: The coffeepot's handle can break, causing the pot to fall. Consumers can suffer burn injuries from hot coffee or lacerations from broken glass.
distribution: Tim Hortons coffeeshops in Kentucky, Ohio, Maine, Michigan, New York, and West Virginia sold the coffeemakers, from October 1999 through February 2000, for about $65.
hazards: The coffeepot's handle can break, causing the pot to fall. Consumers can suffer burn injuries from hot coffee or lacerations from broken glass.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the coffeepots immediately. Consumers should contact Tim Hortons for instructions on receiving a replacement coffeepot and $5 gift certificate.
injuries: Tim Hortons has received 150 reports of handles breaking off of the coffeepots, resulting in nine burn injuries.

title: CPSC, DEWALT® Industrial Tool Co. Announce Recall of 18-Volt Battery Packs
reason: The battery packs' clips can come loose, causing the battery packs to fall. When working with these tools, falling battery packs weighing about 2.2 pounds can cause injury.
firm: DEWALT® Industrial Tool Co., of Baltimore, Md.
distribution: Major home centers and hardware stores, as well as industrial distributors, sold battery packs nationwide, from May 1997 through June 1998, for between $70 and $85.
hazards: The battery packs' clips can come loose, causing the battery packs to fall. When working with these tools, falling battery packs weighing about 2.2 pounds can cause injury.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using the battery packs, and call DEWALT® for a free repair kit.
injuries: DEWALT® has received 53 reports of battery packs falling from tools. There have been five reports of injuries, including a battery pack striking a consumer on the head.

title: CPSC, Frieder Inc. Announce Recall of Power Strips
reason: The wiring in these power strips is undersized and poses shock, electrocution and fire hazards.
distribution: Discount outlets nationwide sold the power strips, from January 1997 through July 1998, for about $3.
hazards: The wiring in these power strips is undersized and poses shock, electrocution and fire hazards.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these power strips and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or send them to Frieder for a refund plus postage.

title: CPSC, Dynacraft Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Mountain Bikes
reason: The front suspension forks on these bikes might not have been welded properly, and can break apart during use, resulting in serious injury to the rider.
distribution: Target stores nationwide sold these mountain bikes from November 1999 through February 2000 for about $140.
hazards: The front suspension forks on these bikes might not have been welded properly, and can break apart during use, resulting in serious injury to the rider.
remedies: Stop riding these bikes immediately and take them to the Target store where purchased, for a choice of a free replacement fork or a free replacement bike.
injuries: Dynacraft has received eight reports of injury to riders when the front forks on these bikes broke apart. Injuries included cuts, bruises, back strain and chipped and lost teeth.

title: CPSC, Cadet Recall In-Wall Heaters; Settle Lawsuit
product: Cadet and Encore in-wall electric heaters
reason: Flames, sparks or molten particles can spew through the front grill cover of the heater into the living area of a residence, putting consumers at risk from fires, including burn injuries, smoke inhalation and property damage. The heaters also can become energized creating a risk of electric shock.
firm: Cadet Manufacturing Co., of Vancouver, Wash.
distribution: These heaters were distributed mainly in California, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington.
hazards: Flames, sparks or molten particles can spew through the front grill cover of the heater into the living area of a residence, putting consumers at risk from fires, including burn injuries, smoke inhalation and property damage. The heaters also can become energized creating a risk of electric shock.
remedies: Cadet is offering consumers replacement heaters at a significantly reduced cost. Each heater will cost between $25 and $57, depending on the model. Consumers who already have replaced the recalled units from October 23, 1997, until today can file a claim for partial reimbursement for $25 per heater. Consumers must register to participate in this recall by February 17, 2002.
injuries: CPSC is aware of more than 320 reports of heaters that smoked, sparked, caught fire, emitted flames, or ejected burning particles or molten materials. These incidents have allegedly resulted in three deaths, two serious burn injuries and property damage claims exceeding $1.2 million, which include five partial or total house fires.

title: CPSC, TSI Prime Inc. Announce Recall of Ceiling Light Fixtures
reason: The light fixtures can short circuit, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Wal-Mart and Lowe's stores nationwide sold the light fixtures for between $16 and $25. Wal-Mart sold the fixtures individually packaged from February 1998 through March 1999. Lowe's sold the fixtures in two-packs from January 1998 through January 2000.
hazards: The light fixtures can short circuit, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these lights immediately, and call TSI Prime, to arrange for a free replacement.
injuries: TSI Prime has received three reports of these light fixtures short circuiting, resulting in scorch marks on ceilings. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Mountain High Hosiery Ltd. Announce Recall of Tommy Hilfiger Socks for Infants and Children
product: Tommy Hilfiger socks for infants and children
reason: The heat-sealed Tommy Hilfiger flag logo appliques on these socks can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
firm: Mountain High Hosiery Ltd., of San Diego, Calif.
distribution: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold two-pair packages of the socks, from January 1999 through January 2000, for about $10.
hazards: The heat-sealed Tommy Hilfiger flag logo appliques on these socks can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these socks immediately, and call Mountain High to receive an exchange or a refund.
injuries: Mountain High has received three reports of the logo appliques detaching from these socks. No injuries have been reported

title: CPSC, Nordstrom Inc. Announce Recall of Infant and Toddler Jackets
reason: Snaps located on the flap pockets of these jackets could be removed, presenting a choking hazard to infants and young children.
distribution: Nordstrom stores nationwide sold these jackets, during January 2000, for about $34 to $36.
hazards: Snaps located on the flap pockets of these jackets could be removed, presenting a choking hazard to infants and young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these jackets immediately and return them to any Nordstrom store, for a refund.

title: In Wake of Second Death, CPSC and Burger King Again Urge Consumers to Destroy and Discard Pokemon Balls
product: Pokémon balls distributed with Burger King kids meals
reason: The balls pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age.
distribution: Burger King restaurants nationwide distributed the Pokémon balls inside Burger King big kids meals and regular kids meals from early November through December 1999.
hazards: The balls pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the balls away from children under the age of three. They should discard the ball or return both halves of the ball and the clip to a Burger King restaurant for a free order of small fries. Children can continue to use the Pokémon toy that came inside the ball.
injuries: On January 25, 2000, a 4-month-old boy in Indianapolis, Ind., reportedly suffocated when one-half of a Pokémon ball that was in his crib became stuck on his face. In December, a 13-month-old girl reportedly suffocated when one-half of a Pokémon ball covered her nose and mouth. Also in December, an 18-month-old girl nearly suffocated when a ball-half got stuck over her face. On the second attempt, the girl's father was able to pull the ball-half from her face.
